verses.zh: 保罗定睛看着公会的人，说：「弟兄们，我在　神面前行事为人都是凭着良心，直到今日。」
verses.en: Paul looked directly[NOTE:1] at the council[NOTE:2] and said, “Brothers, I have lived my life with a clear conscience[NOTE:3] before God to this day.”
notes: Grk “Paul, looking directly at the council, said.” The participle ἀτενίσας (atenisas) has been translated as a finite verb due to requirements of contemporary English style.
Grk “the Sanhedrin” (the Sanhedrin was the highest legal, legislative, and judicial body among the Jews).
BDAG 846 s.v. πολιτεύομαι 3 has “W. a double dat. συνειδήσει ἀγαθῇ πεπολίτευμαι τῷ θεῷ I have lived my life with a clear conscience before God Ac 23:1.”

verses.zh: 大祭司亚拿尼亚就吩咐旁边站着的人打他的嘴。
verses.en: At that[NOTE:1] the high priest Ananias ordered those standing near[NOTE:2] Paul[NOTE:3] to strike[NOTE:4] him on the mouth.
notes: Grk “and” (δέ, de); the phrase “at that” has been used in the translation to clarify the cause and effect relationship.
BDAG 778 s.v. παρίστημι/παριστάνω 2.b.α has “οἱ παρεστῶτες αὐτῷ those standing near him Ac 23:2.”
Grk “him”; the referent (Paul) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Or “hit” (“strike” maintains the wordplay with the following verse). The action was probably designed to indicate a rejection of Paul’s claim to a clear conscience in the previous verse.

verses.zh: 保罗对他说：「你这粉饰的墙，　神要打你！你坐堂为的是按律法审问我，你竟违背律法，吩咐人打我吗？」
verses.en: Then Paul said to him, “God is going to strike you, you whitewashed wall![NOTE:1] Do[NOTE:2] you sit there judging me according to the law,[NOTE:3] and in violation of the law[NOTE:4] you order me to be struck?”
notes: You whitewashed wall. This was an idiom for hypocrisy—just as the wall was painted on the outside but something different on the inside, so this person was not what he appeared or pretended to be (L&N 88.234; see also BDAG 1010 s.v. τοῖχος). Paul was claiming that the man’s response was two-faced (Ezek 13:10-16; Matt 23:27-28). See also Deut 28:22.
Grk “And do.” Because of the difference between Greek style, which often begins sentences or clauses with “and,” and English style, which generally does not, καί (kai) has not been translated here.
The law refers to the law of Moses.

In violation of the law. Paul was claiming that punishment was given before the examination was complete (m. Sanhedrin 3:6-8). Luke’s noting of this detail shows how quickly the leadership moved to react against Paul.tn BDAG 769 s.v. παρανομέω has “παρανομῶν κελεύεις in violation of the law you order Ac 23:3.”

verses.zh: 站在旁边的人说：「你辱骂　神的大祭司吗？」
verses.en: Those standing near him[NOTE:1] said, “Do you dare insult[NOTE:2] God’s high priest?”
notes: The word “him” is not in the Greek text but is implied.

L&N 33.393 has for λοιδορέω (loidoreō) “to speak in a highly insulting manner—‘to slander, to insult strongly, slander, insult.’”sn Insult God’s high priest. Paul was close to violation of the Mosaic law with his response, as the citation from Exod 22:28 in v. 5 makes clear.

verses.zh: 保罗说：「弟兄们，我不晓得他是大祭司；经上记着说：『不可毁谤你百姓的官长。』」
verses.en: Paul replied,[NOTE:1] “I did not realize,[NOTE:2] brothers, that he was the high priest, for it is written, ‘You must not speak evil about a ruler of your people.’”[NOTE:3]
notes: Grk “said.”
Or “know.”
A quotation from Exod 22:28. This text defines a form of blasphemy. Paul, aware of the fact that he came close to crossing the line, backed off out of respect for the law.

verses.zh: 保罗看出大众一半是撒都该人，一半是法利赛人，就在公会中大声说：「弟兄们，我是法利赛人，也是法利赛人的子孙。我现在受审问，是为盼望死人复活。」
verses.en: Then when Paul noticed[NOTE:1] that part of them were Sadducees[NOTE:2] and the others Pharisees,[NOTE:3] he shouted out in the council,[NOTE:4] “Brothers, I am a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees. I am on trial concerning the hope of the resurrection[NOTE:5] of the dead!”
notes: BDAG 200 s.v. γινώσκω 4 has “to be aware of someth., perceive, notice, realize”; this is further clarified by section 4.c: “w. ὅτι foll….Ac 23:6.”
See the note on Sadducees in 4:1.
See the note on Pharisee in 5:34.
Grk “the Sanhedrin” (the Sanhedrin was the highest legal, legislative, and judicial body among the Jews).

That is, concerning the hope that the dead will be resurrected. Grk “concerning the hope and resurrection.” BDAG 320 s.v. ἐλπίς 1.b.α states, “Of Israel’s messianic hope Ac 23:6 (ἐ. καὶ ἀνάστασις for ἐ. τῆς ἀν. [obj. gen] as 2 Macc 3:29 ἐ. καὶ σωτηρία).” With an objective genitive construction, the resurrection of the dead would be the “object” of the hope.

verses.zh: 说了这话，法利赛人和撒都该人就争论起来，会众分为两党。
verses.en: When he said this,[NOTE:1] an argument[NOTE:2] began[NOTE:3] between the Pharisees and the Sadducees, and the assembly was divided.
notes: The participle εἰπόντος (eipontos) has been translated temporally.
Or “a dispute” (BDAG 940 s.v. στάσις 3).
Grk “there came about an argument.” This has been simplified to “an argument began”

verses.zh: 因为撒都该人说，没有复活，也没有天使和鬼魂；法利赛人却说，两样都有。
verses.en: (For the Sadducees say there is no resurrection, or angel, or spirit, but the Pharisees acknowledge them all.)[NOTE:1]
notes: BDAG 55 s.v. ἀμφότεροι 2 has “all, even when more than two are involved…Φαρισαῖοι ὁμολογοῦσιν τὰ ἀ. believe in them all 23:8.” On this belief see Josephus, J. W. 2.8.14 (2.163); Ant. 18.1.3 (18.14).sn This is a parenthetical note by the author.

verses.zh: 于是大大地喧嚷起来。有几个法利赛党的文士站起来争辩说：「我们看不出这人有甚么恶处，倘若有鬼魂或是天使对他说过话，怎么样呢？」
verses.en: There was a great commotion,[NOTE:1] and some experts in the law[NOTE:2] from the party of the Pharisees stood up[NOTE:3] and protested strongly,[NOTE:4] “We find nothing wrong[NOTE:5] with this man. What if a spirit or an angel has spoken to him?”
notes: Or “clamor” (cf. BDAG 565 s.v. κραυγή 1.a, which has “there arose a loud outcry” here, and Exod 12:30).
Or “and some scribes.” See the note on the phrase “experts in the law” in 4:5.
Grk “standing up.” The participle ἀναστάντες (anastantes) has been translated as a finite verb due to requirements of contemporary English style.

Grk “protested strongly, saying.” L&N 39.27 has “διαμάχομαι: to fight or contend with, involving severity and thoroughness—‘to protest strongly, to contend with.’…‘some scribes from the party of the Pharisees protested strongly’ Ac 23:9.” The participle λέγοντες (legontes) is redundant and has not been translated.
“We find nothing wrong with this man.” Here is another declaration of innocence. These leaders recognized the possibility that Paul might have the right to make his claim.

verses.zh: 那时大起争吵，千夫长恐怕保罗被他们扯碎了，就吩咐兵丁下去，把他从众人当中抢出来，带进营楼去。
verses.en: When the argument became[NOTE:1] so great the commanding officer[NOTE:2] feared that they would tear Paul to pieces,[NOTE:3] he ordered the detachment[NOTE:4] to go down, take him away from them by force,[NOTE:5] and bring him into the barracks.[NOTE:6]
notes: This genitive absolute construction with the participle γινομένης (ginomenēs) has been taken temporally (it could also be translated as causal).

Grk “the chiliarch” (an officer in command of a thousand soldiers). In Greek the term χιλίαρχος (chiliarchos) literally described the “commander of a thousand,” but it was used as the standard translation for the Latin tribunus militum or tribunus militare, the military tribune who commanded a cohort of 600 men.

Grk “that Paul would be torn to pieces by them.” BDAG 236 s.v. διασπάω has “of an angry mob μὴ διασπασθῇ ὁ Παῦλος ὑπ᾿ αὐτῶν that Paul would be torn in pieces by them Ac 23:10.” The passive construction is somewhat awkward in English and has been converted to an equivalent active construction in the translation.

Normally this term means “army,” but according to BDAG 947 s.v. στράτευμα, “Of a smaller detachment of soldiers, sing. Ac 23:10, 27.” In the plural it can be translated “troops,” but it is singular here.
Or “to go down, grab him out of their midst.”
Or “the headquarters.” BDAG 775 s.v. παρεμβολή 2 has “barracks/headquarters of the Roman troops in Jerusalem Ac 21:34, 37; 22:24; 23:10, 16, 32.”

verses.zh: 当夜，主站在保罗旁边，说：「放心吧！你怎样在耶路撒冷为我作见证，也必怎样在罗马为我作见证。」
verses.en: The following night the Lord[NOTE:1] stood near[NOTE:2] Paul[NOTE:3] and said, “Have courage,[NOTE:4] for just as you have testified about me in Jerusalem,[NOTE:5] so you must also testify in Rome.”[NOTE:6]
notes: The presence of the Lord indicated the vindicating presence and direction of God.
Grk “standing near Paul, said.” The participle ἐπιστάς (epistas) has been translated as a finite verb due to requirements of contemporary English style.
Grk “him”; the referent (Paul) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Or “Do not be afraid.”
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

Like Jesus went to Jerusalem, Paul would now go to Rome. This trip forms the concluding backdrop to Acts. This is the second notice about going to Rome (see Acts 19:21 for the first).map For location see JP4-A1.

verses.zh: 到了天亮，犹太人同谋起誓，说：「若不先杀保罗就不吃不喝。」
verses.en: When morning came,[NOTE:1] the Jews formed[NOTE:2] a conspiracy[NOTE:3] and bound themselves with an oath[NOTE:4] not to eat or drink anything[NOTE:5] until they had killed Paul.
notes: Grk “when it was day.”
Grk “forming a conspiracy, bound.” The participle ποιήσαντες (poiēsantes) has been translated as a finite verb due to requirements of contemporary English style.

L&N 30.72 has ‘some Jews formed a conspiracy’ Ac 23:12”; BDAG 979 s.v. συστροφή 1 has “Judeans came together in a mob 23:12. But in the last pass. the word may also mean—2. the product of a clandestine gathering, plot, conspiracy” (see also Amos 7:10; Ps 63:3).

Or “bound themselves under a curse.” BDAG 63 s.v. ἀναθεματίζω 1 has “trans. put under a curse τινά someone…pleonastically ἀναθέματι ἀ. ἑαυτόν Ac 23:14…ἀ. ἑαυτόν vss. 12, 21, 13 v.l.” On such oaths see m. Shevi’it 3:1-5. The participle λέγοντες (legontes) is redundant in English and has not been translated.
The word “anything” is not in the Greek text, but is implied. Direct objects were often omitted in Greek when clear from the context, but must be supplied for the modern English reader.

verses.zh: 这样同心起誓的有四十多人。
verses.en: There were more than forty of them who formed this conspiracy.[NOTE:1]
notes: L&N 30.73 defines συνωμοσία (sunōmosia) as “a plan for taking secret action someone or some institution, with the implication of an oath binding the conspirators—‘conspiracy, plot.’…‘there were more than forty of them who formed this conspiracy’ Ac 23:13.”

verses.zh: 他们来见祭司长和长老，说：「我们已经起了一个大誓，若不先杀保罗就不吃甚么。
verses.en: They[NOTE:1] went[NOTE:2] to the chief priests[NOTE:3] and the elders and said, “We have bound ourselves with a solemn oath[NOTE:4] not to partake[NOTE:5] of anything until we have killed Paul.
notes: Grk “who.” Because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, the relative pronoun (“whom”) was translated by the third person plural pronoun (“them”) and a new sentence begun in the translation.
Grk “going.” The participle προσελθόντες (proselthontes) has been translated as a finite verb due to requirements of contemporary English style.

They went to the chief priests. The fact that the high priest knew of this plot and did nothing shows the Jewish leadership would even become accomplices to murder to stop Paul. They would not allow Roman justice to take its course. Paul’s charge in v. 3 of superficially following the law is thus shown to be true.

Or “bound ourselves under a curse.” BDAG 63 s.v. ἀναθεματίζω 1 has “trans. put under a curse τινά someone…pleonastically ἀναθέματι ἀ. ἑαυτόν Ac 23:14…ἀ. ἑαυτόν vss. 12, 21, 13 v.l.” The pleonastic use ἀναθέματι ἀνεθεματίσαμεν (literally “we have cursed ourselves with a curse”) probably serves as an intensifier following Semitic usage, and is represented in the translation by the word “solemn.” On such oaths see m. Nedarim 3:1, 3.
This included both food and drink (γεύομαι [geuomai] is used of water turned to wine in John 2:9).

verses.zh: 现在你们和公会要知会千夫长，叫他带下保罗到你们这里来，假作要详细察考他的事；我们已经预备好了，不等他来到跟前就杀他。」
verses.en: So now you and the council[NOTE:1] request the commanding officer[NOTE:2] to bring him down to you, as if you were going to determine[NOTE:3] his case[NOTE:4] by conducting a more thorough inquiry.[NOTE:5] We are ready to kill him[NOTE:6] before he comes near this place.”[NOTE:7]
notes: Grk “the Sanhedrin” (the Sanhedrin was the highest legal, legislative, and judicial body among the Jews).
Grk “the chiliarch” (an officer in command of a thousand soldiers). See note on the term “commanding officer” in v. 10.
Or “decide.” BDAG 227 s.v. διαγινώσκω has “ἀκριβέστερον τὰ περὶ αὐτοῦ to make a more thorough examination of his case Ac 23:15.”
Grk “determine the things about him.”
The expression “more thorough inquiry” reflects the comparative form of ἀκριβέστερον (akribesteron).
“We are ready to kill him.” Now those Jews involved in the conspiracy, along with the leaders as accomplices, are going to break one of the ten commandments.
The words “this place” are not in the Greek text, but are implied.

verses.zh: 保罗的外甥听见他们设下埋伏，就来到营楼里告诉保罗。
verses.en: But when the son of Paul’s sister heard about the ambush,[NOTE:1] he came and entered[NOTE:2] the barracks[NOTE:3] and told Paul.
notes: Or “plot” (BDAG 334 s.v. ἐνέδρα).
Grk “coming and entering…, he told.” The participles παραγενόμενος (paragenomenos) and εἰσελθών (eiselthōn) have been translated as finite verbs due to requirements of contemporary English style.
Or “the headquarters.” BDAG 775 s.v. παρεμβολή 2 has “barracks/headquarters of the Roman troops in Jerusalem Ac 21:34, 37; 22:24; 23:10, 16, 32.”

verses.zh: 保罗请一个百夫长来，说：「你领这少年人去见千夫长，他有事告诉他。」
verses.en: Paul called[NOTE:1] one of the centurions[NOTE:2] and said, “Take this young man to the commanding officer,[NOTE:3] for he has something to report to him.”
notes: Grk “calling…Paul said.” The participle προσκαλεσάμενος (proskalesamenos) has been translated as a finite verb due to requirements of contemporary English style.
See the note on the word centurion in 10:1.
Grk “the chiliarch” (an officer in command of a thousand soldiers). See note on the term “commanding officer” in v. 10.

verses.zh: 于是把他领去见千夫长，说：「被囚的保罗请我到他那里，求我领这少年人来见你；他有事告诉你。」
verses.en: So the centurion[NOTE:1] took him and brought him to the commanding officer[NOTE:2] and said, “The prisoner Paul called[NOTE:3] me and asked me to bring this young man to you because he has something to tell you.”
notes: Grk “he”; the referent (the centurion) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Grk “the chiliarch” (an officer in command of a thousand soldiers). See note on the term “commanding officer” in v. 10.
Grk “calling.” The participle προσκαλεσάμενος (proskalesamenos) has been translated as a finite verb due to requirements of contemporary English style.

verses.zh: 千夫长就拉着他的手，走到一旁，私下问他说：「你有甚么事告诉我呢？」
verses.en: The commanding officer[NOTE:1] took him by the hand, withdrew privately, and asked, “What is it that you want[NOTE:2] to report to me?”
notes: Grk “the chiliarch” (an officer in command of a thousand soldiers). See note on the term “commanding officer” in v. 10.

Grk “you have,” but the expression “have to report” in English could be understood to mean “must report” rather than “possess to report.” For this reason the nearly equivalent expression “want to report,” which is not subject to misunderstanding, was used in the translation.

verses.zh: 他说：「犹太人已经约定，要求你明天带下保罗到公会里去，假作要详细查问他的事。
verses.en: He replied,[NOTE:1] “The Jews have agreed to ask you to bring Paul down to the council[NOTE:2] tomorrow, as if they were going to inquire more thoroughly about him.
notes: Grk “He said.”
Grk “the Sanhedrin” (the Sanhedrin was the highest legal, legislative, and judicial body among the Jews).

verses.zh: 你切不要随从他们；因为他们有四十多人埋伏，已经起誓说：若不先杀保罗就不吃不喝。现在预备好了，只等你应允。」
verses.en: So do not let them persuade you to do this[NOTE:1] because more than forty of them[NOTE:2] are lying in ambush[NOTE:3] for him. They[NOTE:4] have bound themselves with an oath[NOTE:5] not to eat or drink anything[NOTE:6] until they have killed him, and now they are ready, waiting for you to agree to their request.”[NOTE:7]
notes: Grk “do not be persuaded by them.” The passive construction μὴ πεισθῇς αὐτοῖς (mē peisthēs autois) has been converted to an active construction in the translation, and the phrase “to do this” supplied to indicate more clearly the object of their persuasion.
Grk “forty men of them.” In the expression ἐξ αὐτῶν ἄνδρες (ex autōn andres) “men” is somewhat redundant and has not been included in the English translation.
Grk “are lying in wait for him” (BDAG 334 s.v. ἐνεδρεύω); see also v. 16.

Grk “for him, who.” Because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, the relative pronoun (“who”) was translated by the third person plural pronoun (“they”) and a new sentence begun in the translation.
Or “bound themselves under a curse.” BDAG 63 s.v. ἀναθεματίζω 1 has “trans. put under a curse τινά someone…ἀ. ἑαυτόν vss. 12, 21, 13 v.l.”
The word “anything” is not in the Greek text, but is implied. Direct objects were often omitted in Greek when clear from the context, but must be supplied for the modern English reader.

Grk “waiting for your approval,” “waiting for your agreement.” Since it would be possible to misunderstand the literal translation “waiting for your approval” to mean that the Jews were waiting for the commander’s approval to carry out their plot or to kill Paul (as if he were to be an accomplice to their plot), the object of the commander’s approval (their request to bring Paul to the council) has been specified in the translation as “their request.”

verses.zh: 于是千夫长打发少年人走，嘱咐他说：「不要告诉人你将这事报给我了。」
verses.en: Then the commanding officer[NOTE:1] sent the young man away, directing him,[NOTE:2] “Tell no one that you have reported[NOTE:3] these things to me.”
notes: Grk “the chiliarch” (an officer in command of a thousand soldiers). See note on the term “commanding officer” in v. 10.

BDAG 760 s.v. παραγγέλλω has “to make an announcement about someth. that must be done, give orders, command, instruct, direct of all kinds of persons in authority, worldly rulers, Jesus, the apostles…παραγγέλλειν w. an inf. and μή comes to mean forbid to do someth.: π. τινί w. aor. inf. Lk 5:14; 8:56; without the dat., which is easily supplied fr. the context Ac 23:22.” However, if the direct discourse which follows is to be retained in the translation, a different translation must be used since it is awkward to introduce direct discourse with the verb to forbid. Thus the alternative to direct was used.
On this verb, see BDAG 325-26 s.v. ἐμφανίζω 2. The term was frequently used of an official report to authorities. In modern terms, this was a police tip.

verses.zh: 千夫长便叫了两个百夫长来，说：「预备步兵二百，马兵七十，长枪手二百，今夜亥初往凯撒利亚去；
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] he summoned[NOTE:2] two of the centurions[NOTE:3] and said, “Make ready 200 soldiers to go to Caesarea[NOTE:4] along with 70 horsemen[NOTE:5] and 200 spearmen[NOTE:6] by[NOTE:7] nine o’clock tonight,[NOTE:8]
notes: Grk “And.” Since this represents a response to the reported ambush, καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the logical sequence.
Grk “summoning…he said.” The participle προσκαλεσάμενος (proskalesamenos) has been translated as a finite verb due to requirements of contemporary English style.
See the note on the word centurion in 10:1.

For location see Map2-C1; Map4-B3; Map5-F2; Map7-A1; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.sn Caesarea was a city on the coast of Palestine south of Mount Carmel (not Caesarea Philippi). See the note on Caesarea in Acts 10:1. This was a journey of about 65 mi (just over 100 km).
Or “cavalrymen.”

200 soldiers…along with 70 horsemen and 200 spearmen. The resulting force assembled to guard Paul was almost a full cohort. The Roman commander was taking no chances, but was sending the issue up the chain of command to the procurator to decide.tn A military technical term of uncertain meaning. BDAG 217 s.v. δεξιολάβος states, “a word of uncertain mng., military t.t., acc. to Joannes Lydus…and Theophyl. Sim., Hist. 4, 1 a light-armed soldier, perh. bowman, slinger; acc. to a scholion in CMatthaei p. 342 body-guard….Spearman Goodspd., NRSV; ‘security officer’, GDKilpatrick, JTS 14, ’63, 393f.”
Grk “from.”
Grk “from the third hour of the night.”

verses.zh: 也要预备牲口叫保罗骑上，护送到巡抚腓力斯那里去。」
verses.en: and provide mounts for Paul to ride[NOTE:1] so that he may be brought safely to Felix[NOTE:2] the governor.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Grk “provide mounts to put Paul on.”sn Mounts for Paul to ride. The fact they were riding horses indicates they wanted everyone to move as quickly as possible.

Felix the governor was Antonius Felix, a freedman of Antonia, mother of the Emperor Claudius. He was the brother of Pallas and became procurator of Palestine in a.d. 52/53. His administration was notorious for its corruption, cynicism, and cruelty. According to the historian Tacitus (History 5.9) Felix “reveled in cruelty and lust, and wielded the power of a king with the mind of a slave.”
Grk “Felix the procurator.” The official Roman title has been translated as “governor” (BDAG 433 s.v. ἡγεμών 2).

verses.zh: 千夫长又写了文书，
verses.en: He wrote[NOTE:1] a letter that went like this:[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “writing.” Due to the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, a new sentence was begun here in the translation, supplying “he” (referring to the commanding officer, Claudius Lysias) as subject. The participle γράψας (grapsas) has been translated as a finite verb due to requirements of contemporary English style.

Grk “having this form,” “having this content.” L&N 33.48 has “γράψσς ἐπιστολὴν ἔχουσαν τὸν τύπον τοῦτον ‘then he wrote a letter that went like this’ Ac 23:25. It is also possible to understand ἐπιστολή in Ac 23:25 not as a content or message, but as an object (see 6.63).”

verses.zh: 大略说：「克劳第•吕西亚，请巡抚腓力斯大人安。
verses.en: Claudius Lysias to His Excellency Governor[NOTE:1] Felix,[NOTE:2] greetings.
notes: Grk “Procurator.” The official Roman title has been translated as “governor” (BDAG 433 s.v. ἡγεμών 2).
Governor Felix. See the note on Felix in v. 24.

verses.zh: 这人被犹太人拿住，将要杀害，我得知他是罗马人，就带兵丁下去救他出来。
verses.en: This man was seized[NOTE:1] by the Jews and they were about to kill him,[NOTE:2] when I came up[NOTE:3] with the detachment[NOTE:4] and rescued him because I had learned that he was[NOTE:5] a Roman citizen.[NOTE:6]
notes: The participle συλλημφθέντα (sullēmphthenta) has been translated as a finite verb due to requirements of contemporary English style. The remark reviews events of Acts 21:27-40.
Grk “and was about to be killed by them.” The passive construction has been converted to an active one in the translation for stylistic reasons.
Or “approached.”

Normally this term means “army,” but according to BDAG 947 s.v. στράτευμα, “Of a smaller detachment of soldiers, sing. Ac 23:10, 27.” In the plural it can be translated “troops,” but it is singular here.
In Greek this is a present tense retained in indirect discourse.

The letter written by the Roman commander Claudius Lysias was somewhat self-serving. He made it sound as if the rescue of a Roman citizen had been a conscious act on his part. In fact, he had made the discovery of Paul’s Roman citizenship somewhat later. See Acts 21:37-39 and 22:24-29.tn The word “citizen” is supplied here for emphasis and clarity.

verses.zh: 因要知道他们告他的缘故，我就带他下到他们的公会去，
verses.en: Since I wanted to know[NOTE:1] what charge they were accusing him of,[NOTE:2] I brought him down to their council.[NOTE:3]
notes: Or “determine.”

Grk “to know the charge on account of which they were accusing him.” This has been simplified to eliminate the prepositional phrase and relative pronoun δι᾿ ἣν (di’ hēn) similar to L&N 27.8 which has “‘I wanted to find out what they were accusing him of, so I took him down to their Council’ Ac 23:28.”
Grk “their Sanhedrin” (the Sanhedrin was the highest legal, legislative, and judicial body among the Jews).

verses.zh: 便查知他被告是因他们律法的辩论，并没有甚么该死该绑的罪名。
verses.en: I found he[NOTE:1] was accused with reference to controversial questions[NOTE:2] about their law, but no charge against him deserved death or imprisonment.[NOTE:3]
notes: Grk “whom I found.” Because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, the relative pronoun (“whom”) has been changed to a personal pronoun (“he”) and a new sentence begun in the translation at this point.

With reference to controversial questions. Note how the “neutral” Roman authorities saw the issue. This was a religious rather than a civil dispute. See Acts 18:15.tn BDAG 428 s.v. ζήτημα states, “in our lit. only in Ac, w. the mng. it still has in Mod. Gk. (controversial) question, issue, argument…Ac 15:2; 26:3. ζ. περί τινος questions about someth.…18:15; 25:19.—In 23:29, since περί had already been used, the subj. of the discussion is added in the gen. ζ. τοῦ νόμου αὐτῶν.”

Despite the official assessment that no charge against him deserved death or imprisonment, there was no effort to release Paul.tn Grk “but having no charge worthy of death or imprisonment.” BDAG 273-74 s.v. ἔγκλημα 1 has “legal t.t.…ἔ. ἄξιον θανάτου ἢ δεσμῶν a charge deserving death or imprisonment 23:29.”

verses.zh: 后来有人把要害他的计谋告诉我，我就立时解他到你那里去，又吩咐告他的人在你面前告他。（有古卷加：愿你平安！）」
verses.en: When I was informed[NOTE:1] there would be a plot[NOTE:2] against this man, I sent him to you at once, also ordering his accusers to state their charges[NOTE:3] against him before you.
notes: Grk “It being revealed to me.” The participle μηνυθείσης (mēnutheisēs) has been taken temporally.
The term translated “plot” here is a different one than the one in Acts 23:16 (see BDAG 368 s.v. ἐπιβουλή).

Grk “the things against him.” This could be rendered as “accusations,” “grievances,” or “charges,” but since “ordered his accusers to state their accusations” sounds redundant in English, “charges” was used instead.

verses.zh: 于是，兵丁照所吩咐他们的，将保罗夜里带到安提帕底。
verses.en: So the soldiers, in accordance with their orders,[NOTE:1] took[NOTE:2] Paul and brought him to Antipatris[NOTE:3] during the night.
notes: BDAG 237-38 s.v. διατάσσω 2 has “κατὰ τὸ δ. αὐτοῖς in accordance w. their orders…Ac 23:31.”
Grk “taking.” The participle ἀναλαβόντες (analabontes) has been translated as a finite verb due to requirements of contemporary English style.
Antipatris was a city in Judea about 35 mi (55 km) northwest of Jerusalem (about halfway to Caesarea). It was mentioned several times by Josephus (Ant. 13.15.1 [13.390]; J. W. 1.4.7 [1.99]).

verses.zh: 第二天，让马兵护送，他们就回营楼去。
verses.en: The next day they let[NOTE:1] the horsemen[NOTE:2] go on with him, and they returned to the barracks.[NOTE:3]
notes: Grk “letting.” The participle ἐάσαντες (easantes) has been translated as a finite verb due to requirements of contemporary English style.
Or “cavalrymen.”
Or “the headquarters.” BDAG 775 s.v. παρεμβολή 2 has “barracks/headquarters of the Roman troops in Jerusalem Ac 21:34, 37; 22:24; 23:10, 16, 32.”

verses.zh: 马兵来到凯撒利亚，把文书呈给巡抚，便叫保罗站在他面前。
verses.en: When the horsemen[NOTE:1] came to Caesarea[NOTE:2] and delivered the letter to the governor, they also presented[NOTE:3] Paul to him.
notes: Grk “who, coming to Caesarea.” Because of the length and complexity of the Greek construction, a new sentence was begun here in the translation. The relative pronoun (“who”) has been replaced with the referent (the horsemen) in the translation for clarity.
Caesarea was a city on the coast of Palestine south of Mount Carmel (not Caesarea Philippi). See the note on Caesarea in Acts 10:1. It was about 30 mi (50 km) from Antipatris.
BDAG 778 s.v. παρίστημι/παριστάνω 1.b has “present, represent—α. lit. τινά τινι someone to someone παρέστησαν τὸν Παῦλον αὐτῷ Ac 23:33.”

verses.zh: 巡抚看了文书，问保罗是哪省的人，既晓得他是基利家人，
verses.en: When the governor[NOTE:1] had read[NOTE:2] the letter,[NOTE:3] he asked[NOTE:4] what province he was from.[NOTE:5] When he learned[NOTE:6] that he was from Cilicia,[NOTE:7]
notes: Grk “he”; the referent (the governor) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Grk “having read.” The participle ἀναγνούς (anagnous) has been translated as a finite verb due to requirements of contemporary English style.
The words “the letter” are not in the Greek text but are implied. Direct objects were often omitted in Greek, but must be supplied for the modern English reader.
Grk “and asking.” The participle ἐπερωτήσας (eperōtēsas) has been translated as a finite verb and καί (kai) left untranslated due to requirements of contemporary English style.
Governor Felix asked what province he was from to determine whether he had legal jurisdiction over Paul. He could have sent him to his home province for trial, but decided to hear the case himself.
Grk “and learning.” The participle πυθόμενος (puthomenos) has been translated as a finite verb due to requirements of contemporary English style.
Cilicia was a province in southeastern Asia Minor.

verses.zh: 就说：「等告你的人来到，我要细听你的事」；便吩咐人把他看守在希律的衙门里。
verses.en: he said, “I will give you a hearing[NOTE:1] when your accusers arrive too.” Then[NOTE:2] he ordered that Paul[NOTE:3] be kept under guard in Herod’s palace.[NOTE:4]
notes: Or “I will hear your case.” BDAG 231 s.v. διακούω has “as legal t.t. give someone an opportunity to be heard in court, give someone (τινός) a hearing Ac 23:35”; L&N 56.13 has “to give a judicial hearing in a legal matter—‘to hear a case, to provide a legal hearing, to hear a case in court.’”

Grk “ordering.” The participle κελεύσας (keleusas) has been translated as a finite verb and a new sentence begun here due to the length and complexity of the Greek sentence. “Then” has also been supplied to indicate the logical and temporal sequence.
Grk “him”; the referent (Paul) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Herod’s palace (Grk “Herod’s praetorium”) was the palace built in Caesarea by Herod the Great. See Josephus, Ant. 15.9.6 (15.331). These events belong to the period of a.d. 56-57.
